Nell from the Silt Lanes, Tam says, knows more about the forgetting. But not today: the water is rising.

The journey continues to Varrowmouth. From there, there is no way back to the earlier cities.

Behind you remain cleared rooms and ordinary hearths.

You confirm the journey with no return.
A sailor unhooks the plank between train and ship.

"The lower one belongs to the water within the hour."

The clerk slides a slate towards you. It reads: "Please state only what I can actually verify."
He writes: "The date is the receipt. Not your arrival." Then he uncovers both columns.

Nell from the Silt Lanes, Tam says, knows more about forgetting. And at ebb tide the Wreck Field lies dry, beyond the east pier.

The Tide Council sits on the High Street. It will be a while yet before they let you in.

You don't have to prove anything to anyone.
Osric can explain the burden to you.
„Ich gehe selbst. Du hältst nur die Plan: "I'll walk myself. You just hold the plank." Nell reaches the pilot's room with dry feet. Her name remains her own business.
„Das Kind ist noch da. Die Küche wusste: "The child is still here. The kitchen just no longer knew whose plate it was." Nell counts the portions with one finger. "I don't want the gap to become proof that someone needs nothing."

Osric explains the binding to every name. Nell listens and says: "You can ask me. You can't give the answer for me."

Don't ask for an answer yet.
„Nein. Ich will weitergehen können.“ Du: "No. I want to be able to move on." You hold on to her answer. The other ways out stay open.
„Wenn du bleibst und jeden Namen mit mir: "If you stay and check every name with me, yes. I'm not saying it's easy." You leave the answer open to change until the handover truly begins.

You cross the marked line. Being cut off by the tide does not count as a victory.
